groups.summary: Two distinct referral propagation contracts: direct referrer versus all ancestors.
groups.review_basis: publicly visible source description; original synopsis, not a copied statement or validated oracle

variants.synopsis: Assign sequential account IDs. Adding a referred account credits only its direct referrer. Query up to k accounts meeting a minimum total, ordered by total credit then ID. Credits are nonnegative; the referrer already exists.
Referral credit propagates through every ancestor. The minimum-credit query and total-credit/ID ordering follow the base variant.

groups.summary: Single-mode and mode-switching grid routes must remain separate. Source example inconsistencies need clarification.
groups.review_basis: publicly visible source description; original synopsis, not a copied statement or validated oracle

variants.synopsis: Travel orthogonally from S to D avoiding X, using one transport mode. Minimize total time, then cost. Leaving a mode cell incurs its charge; leaving S is free. Return the selected mode, or an empty string if unreachable.
issues: The first example counts five charged bike blocks; the written departure-cell convention appears to charge four. Do not adopt that example as an oracle.

variants.synopsis: Allow transport-mode changes and minimize the ordered pair of travel time and cost. Return that pair, or [-1,-1] when unreachable.
issues: The example route appears to repeat/count the destination inconsistently. Clarify before deriving tests.

variants.synopsis: Evaluate an IPv4 address against ordered ALLOW/DENY host or CIDR rules. The first matching rule determines the Boolean result; inputs are valid and a match is guaranteed.

leetcode_relationship.evidence: Hack2Hire explicitly describes a variation of LC 751. Firewall rule evaluation differs from decomposing an address range into CIDR blocks.

variants.synopsis: For a prerequisite DAG, every ready unit-duration task starts immediately with unlimited workers. Return tasks that are alone in their execution time frontier, in any order; n is at most 100,000.
